title: Flipkart Minutes Hits 1,000 Dark Stores as Walmart's India Bet Reshapes Quick Commerce
excerpt: Less than two years after launch, Flipkart's quick-delivery arm has built India's second-largest micro-fulfillment network and is targeting 1,500 stores by year-end.
body:
• Flipkart Minutes has reached 1,000 micro-fulfillment centres across 130 cities, less than two years after launching in August 2024, and plans to expand to 1,500 by end of 2026
  • The expansion positions Flipkart as India's second-largest quick-commerce network by dark store count, behind Blinkit's 2,243 centres, according to Jefferies
  • Amazon, Flipkart, and Reliance's combined push into quick commerce has erased over $15 billion in market value from incumbents Eternal (Blinkit parent) and Swiggy
  • India's quick-commerce sector has surpassed $11 billion, with more than 6,000 dark stores now operating nationwide and significant overlap in major cities

From Late Entrant to Second Place

When Flipkart launched its quick-commerce service Minutes in August 2024, it was entering a market already dominated by Blinkit, Zepto, and Swiggy Instamart. Two years on, the Walmart-backed company has built a network of 1,000 micro-fulfillment centres—small, strategically located warehouses designed to enable deliveries within minutes—across more than 130 Indian cities.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=5cY6h73YAKI

Flipkart plans to expand the network to 1,500 centres by the end of 2026, according to TechCrunch. Based on current store counts and announced expansion plans, Flipkart could emerge as India's second-largest quick-commerce network by micro-fulfillment centre count, behind Blinkit which operates 2,243 such centres, according to a Jefferies research note.

"People in smaller cities build a slightly larger average order value basket as they are value conscious."

— Kunal Gupta, Head of Flipkart Minutes

The Small-Town Strategy

Unlike competitors who initially concentrated on metro areas, Flipkart has leaned into smaller towns and cities, which now make up 70% of its footprint. The company has expanded aggressively in eastern states including Bihar—one of India's poorest regions—betting that value-conscious consumers in smaller markets will build larger average order values than their metro counterparts.

https://x.com/Sh0AibAkhter/status/2091402906545324458

The strategy comes as Flipkart prepares for its Mumbai stock exchange listing, making growth metrics and geographic reach critical to its valuation narrative.

The Competitive Pressure

The entry of deep-pocketed global players has rattled the incumbents. Eternal's shares have fallen 28% from their October peak, while Swiggy has declined about 47% from its September high, erasing more than $15 billion in combined market value, according to TradingView data. Macquarie has downgraded Swiggy to Underperform, warning that competitive intensity could last "years, not quarters."

Amazon is accelerating its own push with Amazon Now, currently operating over 500 micro-fulfillment centres in more than 15 cities. CEO Andy Jassy, during a recent India visit, announced plans to expand the service to 300 cities. Reliance Retail, leveraging its network of more than 3,100 stores across 1,200 cities, is strengthening JioMart's quick-commerce operations, adding another well-funded competitor to the market.

A Market That Keeps Growing

India's quick-commerce market has crossed $11 billion, with more than 6,000 dark stores now operational nationwide, according to Bernstein. The sector has reshaped shopping patterns across the world's most populous nation, with companies delivering everything from smartphones to milk within 10 to 30 minutes from neighbourhood warehouses.

Yet profitability remains elusive for most players. Several analysts believe the sector will remain focused on market share over near-term profits. Zepto is preparing for a potential IPO after its unlisted shares declined more than 32% since February, suggesting investor expectations have become more measured even as demand keeps expanding.

What It Means for the Diaspora

For NRI investors watching India's consumer technology sector, the quick-commerce battle represents a defining test of whether global deep pockets (Walmart, Amazon) or local-first players (Blinkit, Zepto) will ultimately dominate. The outcome could reshape e-commerce valuations ahead of several anticipated IPOs, including Flipkart's own listing.
